title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: Post-Issue Corrections of Paper Sets
content:
Some `Bills of Lading and Transport Documents` types are paper sets whose issued originals the line takes back whenever the document is corrected after issue. This page describes the work such a correction involves as a whole: the outcomes it produces, which party brings each about, and the principle that governs each outcome. It is a description of how the parts fit, not a sequence of instructions.

## Scope

The work concerns an issued document of one of those types where a correction of a particular that the type still opens to change has been requested by the documentation party and is registered, while originals of the set in force are in circulation.

## Outcomes and the parties who produce them

A completed correction of this kind leaves four outcomes on the records. Three are record changes made by the desk: the corrected document is in force under a new set number with its originals circulating again; the correction fee of the request sits on the documentation account; and the particular on the document reads as the request asked, the request standing completed. One is the customer's own act: the originals of the old set are shown as handed back at the origin office. That act belongs to the shipper printed on the document; the desk takes it from the documentation party only where that party is the printed shipper, and only at the origin office in a contact during which it has the originals there.

## The principle behind each outcome

- **The new wording on the document.** On these types an issued document may carry corrected wording only while no original of its set in force is still out in circulation. Changing the wording of a document whose old originals are still circulating is exactly what the return requirement exists to prevent.
- **The correction fee.** The fee is a charge on an executed correction, entered once for each request. An entry against a request whose wording is absent from the document would be charging for a correction that is not standing on the document.
- **The corrected set.** A corrected set goes out with its documentation account complete, the fee of the request it carries included, and the request it carries is the one named on that fee entry. Its originals circulate only on a document from which the old set has wholly come back.
- **The handing-back of the originals.** It can take place only while the printed shipper is at the origin office with the originals during the contact. If the originals are not there during the contact, the correction does not move in that contact at all, and the request stays pending, within its return period, for a later contact.

## Timing

Apart from the handing-back, every outcome is a change to the records that the desk makes immediately. Nothing in this work is held up by a delivery, by money clearing, by an approval from outside the desk or by time having to pass.
